newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: MOVE TO SCRAP PRIVATE MEMBERS' EUTHANASIA BILL
National Party M-P, Ian Sinclair, has made a bid to have the private members bill on euthanasia scrapped.
The House of Representatives is due to vote today on Liberal backbencher, Kevin Andrews' private members bill.
But Mr Sinclair, who is opposed to euthanasia, has made a last-minute attempt to have the bill amended into a form that would effectively scrap it.
He says the Andrews' bill is discriminatory because it over-rides the Northern Territory, the A-C-T and Norfolk Island Parliaments.
Mr Sinclair's ammendment calls on the Federal Attorney-General to introduce a new bill which would allow Federal M-Ps to vote on euthanasia in all States and Territories.
His ammendment has been seconded by Liberal M-P and euthanasia supporter Chris Gallus.
DISSENT IN NATIONAL PARTY ON FREE TRADE PUSH
While Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, urges the World Trade Organisation in Singapore to pursue global free trade, not all in his party are happy about it.

The President of the National Party's Moe branch in Victoria, Brian Handley, says the outlook is less than rosy with Australia's share of East Asian imports dropping from four-per-cent, to two-and-a-half-per-cent in the past decade. Mr Handley says Mr Fischer should realise the benefits of free trade are largely illusionary.
50TH ANTARCTIC TRIP
The 50th research expedition sets sail for the Antarctic this afternoon, from Hobart.
The supply ship Aurora Australis is taking 48 expeditioners and a small group of state and federal politicians on a seven-week voyage to all Australian stations.
The ship will drop off expeditioners and supplies at Casey, Davis and Mawson stations before returning by way of Macquarie Island.
The ship's captain, Tim Archer, says unsettled weather could provide some initial challenges, but is genrally expecting a relatively untroubled trip.
PAMPHLETS ON FOOD SAFETY TO BE DISTRIBUTED

The meat industry has launched a Christmas campaign to reduce the rate of illness caused by poor food hygiene. Around one-point-five million Australians contract some type of food-borne illness every year and the number is rising.

The Australian Meat and Lifestock Corporation says as well as improving the safety of food manufacturing, consumers need to realise that over 70 per cent of food poisoning occurs after the time the consumer takes home.
The corporation produced six-million information pamphlets to teach consumers about food safety, which will be distributed in supermarkets.
The food safe campaign is endorsed by the Australian Consumers Asociation and the Australian New Zealand Food Authority.
